stories.title: Contend for the Faith
stories.keyVerse: "Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints."
stories.retelling:
Under the dim glow of the setting sun, Jude, a devoted servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, sat at a small wooden desk. His room was simple, yet filled with an air of purpose. As he picked up his quill, his thoughts swirled like a tempest. His intent had been to write a letter of celebration, a joyful discourse on the shared salvation of the faithful. But an urgent matter pressed upon his heart, compelling him to change course.

Jude sighed deeply, feeling the weight of a responsibility that could not be ignored. He set the quill to parchment, the ink flowing smoothly as he wrote. He opened with a greeting, extending mercy, peace, and love to his readers, hoping to bolster their spirits. Then, with a firm resolve, he turned to the pressing issue. **“Beloved,”** he wrote, **“when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.”**

The words poured out of him like a flood. He described the danger lurking within their community—men who had wormed their way in unnoticed, like shadows creeping across a field at dusk. These were ungodly men, turning the grace of God into a twisted excuse for indulgence and denying the core of their belief, the only Master, Jesus Christ.

Jude’s mind flashed with vivid images as he wrote, each one a historical reminder. The exodus from Egypt, the angels who abandoned their posts, the fiery fate of Sodom and Gomorrah—each a cautionary tale that echoed through the ages. He spoke of the angels, bound in eternal darkness, awaiting judgment for their rebellion. The imagery was stark, as if the very parchment itself was etched with the weight of their fates.

He recalled the celestial dispute between Michael the archangel and the devil over Moses’ body. Michael, though mighty, had not dared to pass judgment himself but said simply, **“The Lord rebuke thee.”** Jude's hand trembled slightly as he wrote this account, the gravity of spiritual warfare resonating deeply.

The letter continued, describing those who rebelled like Cain, who were driven by greed like Balaam, and who defied authority like Korah. Jude likened them to fruitless trees and wild waves, their shame as visible as the foam on the sea.

Yet, amidst the warnings, Jude’s message held hope. He urged his readers to strengthen their faith, to build themselves up, praying in the Holy Spirit. He called them to remain in God’s love, ever watchful for the mercy that leads to eternal life. His plea was simple yet profound: to show compassion to some, to save others with urgency, even as they loathed the corruption that clung to the soul.

As darkness settled outside, Jude’s heart lifted, filled with a sense of fulfillment. He concluded his letter with praise to God, a benediction of glory, majesty, dominion, and power. His task complete, he knew that his words were now in the hands of the faithful, a clarion call echoing in the quiet night.
